newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES GET HAT TRICK FROM UNLIKELY SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES GET HAT TRICK FROM UNLIKELY SOURCE.

text.p: The Phoenix Coyotes got their offence from a most unlikely source on Tuesday as tough guy Jim McKenzie recorded his first career hat trick in a 6-1 rout of the Los Angeles Kings.
McKenzie, who had one goal and 123 penalty minutes in his first 47 games, scored twice in a four-goal first period, much to the delight of his coach and teammates.

"My teammates were laughing after the first and second, then they said there's no rule you can't get four," said McKenzie, who completed his hat trick in the second period two minutes after Matt Johnson scored the lone goal for the Kings.
"Wayne Gretzky McKenzie had a pretty good performance tonight," joked Phoenix coach Don Hay.
Nikolai Khabibulin made 27 saves for Phoenix and Mike Stapleton assisted on all three of McKenzie's goals.
McKenzie reverted back to his regular enforcer role when he engaged in a fight with Johnson late in the second period.
"I should've jumped in and protected our goal scorer, but I saw he was doing okay," Stapleton joked.

At Colorado, Claude Lemieux scored a powerplay goal with four seconds left in overtime as the Avalanche celebrated the return of star centre and captain Joe Sakic with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Bruins.

Sakic, who missed the previous 17 games with a deep laceration in his left calf, sent a shot on the Boston net to pick up an assist on Lemieux's game winner. "I felt great and really excited to get back out there," Sakic said.
Sandis Ozolinsh had a goal and an assist for Colorado.
Ted Donato's 21st goal at 11:08 of the third tied the game for the Bruins, who were 0-for-5 on the powerplay.

In Pittsburgh, Mario Lemieux scored from a near impossible angle with 6:27 left in the third period and added an empty net goal in the final seconds to rally the Penguins to a 4-2 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Glen Murray scored with 12:04 left for the Penguins to tie the game at 2-2 before Lemieux picked up his 40th and 41st goals to seal the victory.
Ken Wregget made 26 saves, including a crucial stop on a Rob Niedermayer shot that started the Pittsburgh break out that led to Murray's tying goal.
"Wregget's save was the key to the game," Lemieux said.
In Buffalo, Ronnie Stern and Aaron Gavey scored 27 seconds apart late in the third period to lift the Calgary Flames to a 5-5 tie with the Sabres.
Calgary extended its unbeaten streak to six games, while Buffalo is unbeaten in 10.
Mike Peca scored his second goal of the game shorthanded just 19 seconds into the third period, and Matthew Barnaby tallied on the power play at 8:51 to give Buffalo a 5-3 lead.
But Stern drove a rebound past Dominik Hasek with 1:54 left in regulation and Gavey chipped a loose puck over Hasek with 1:27 remaining to knot the game.
At Washington, Ron Tugnutt made 31 saves and six different Senators scored as Ottawa crushed the Capitals 6-1.
Tugnutt has been in net for all three Ottawa victories over the Capitals this season, giving up just three goals.
Peter Bondra scored his 36th of the season on the powerplay for Washington 11:07 into the second period to tie the game at 1-1.
Ottawa responded with five unanswered goals. Alexandre Daigle had a goal and two assists and Alexei Yashin set up three scores for the Senators.
In Vancouver, Doug Gilmour and Sergei Berezin each scored twice as the Toronto Maple Leafs took a four-goal third-period lead and held on for a 6-5 victory over the Canucks.
Wendel Clark scored 2:23 into the third period to put Toronto in front 6-2.
Martin Gelinas scored twice in a 2:06 span to get the Canucks within 6-4 and Alexander Mogilny's powerplay goal with 3:58 remaining made it a one-goal game.
But Toronto goaltender Felix Potvin preserved the win with three big saves in the final 30 seconds.
In San Jose, Tony Granato's 16th goal midway through the second period snapped a tie and the Sharks went on to a 3-1 win over the Dallas Stars.
Granato skated across the crease, eluded a stick check by Dallas goaltender Arturs Irbe and, with Irbe out of position, backhanded the puck into the open net.
Jeff Friesen added an empty net goal with 10 seconds left as San Jose beat Dallas for the fourth time in as many meetings this season.
